old: This word names a system where power was said to belong to whoever was born into the right family.
Its Greek roots literally translate to 'rule of the best.'
It ends with the same '-kratíā' root found in words like 'democracy,' both tracing back to Greek krátos, meaning power.
clues: This noun for a privileged social group goes back to Greek words for 'best' and 'power,' so it first described government by the most excellent citizens.
It means a hereditary upper class of titled families, like dukes and countesses, set apart by birth rather than mere wealth. In practice, 'the best' came to mean the best-born.
It ends like democracy and bureaucracy, all built on a Greek word for rule. The French Revolution sent many of its powdered-wig members to the guillotine.
